blocks.text: Design an online auction system, the mechanism behind an English-style auction where a single item is listed for a fixed window of time, competing bidders place bids trying to become the current highest bidder, and whoever holds the highest bid when the auction closes wins and pays. This category has already covered fixed-price commerce at moderate scale and at an extreme, instantaneous scale. This is a fundamentally different shape of problem: price is discovered gradually over an extended time window through genuine competition between bidders, rather than being fixed in advance, and the system has to protect that competition from being unfairly short-circuited in the final seconds.

blocks.alt: Competing bidders submit bids to a proxy bidding engine, which automatically raises the current price to just outbid the loser, and a bid arriving near the closing time extends the auction rather than letting it end unfairly early

blocks.text: The two techniques that define this design are proxy bidding, where a bidder submits a single private maximum and the system automatically bids on their behalf only as much as needed to stay ahead, and anti-sniping time extension, where a bid arriving in the final moments pushes the closing time further out so a determined last-second bidder cannot unfairly end the competition before others can respond.

blocks.text: A seller should be able to list an item with a starting price, a minimum bid increment, and a closing time. A bidder should be able to submit a private maximum bid, with the system automatically bidding on their behalf up to that maximum. Every watcher of an auction should be able to see the current price and who currently holds the highest bid, without ever seeing any bidder's private maximum. A bid arriving close enough to the scheduled closing time should extend that closing time. When an auction closes, the highest bidder should be charged and the seller notified.

blocks.alt: Fair tamper-proof bidding, resistance to last-second sniping, a single consistent current price per item, bids reflected immediately to watchers, and trustworthy payment only on genuine close

blocks.text: Fair, tamper-proof bidding means no bidder should ever be able to see another bidder's private maximum, since knowing it would let them bid exactly one increment above it and win unfairly. Resistance to last-second sniping means a bid placed in the final seconds should not unfairly end the auction before other genuine bidders can respond to it. A single consistent current price means two bidders must never both simultaneously believe they are the current highest bidder for the same item. Bids reflected immediately means everyone watching an auction should see the current price update within a second or two of a new bid landing. And trustworthy payment means only the genuine winning bidder is charged, and only once the auction has actually, definitively closed.

blocks.text: This design assumes a fixed, platform-wide anti-sniping window and extension length for simplicity, though the same underlying mechanism supports per-category configuration equally well. Payment processing is assumed to reuse the payment system this project already covers, triggered only once an auction definitively closes with a genuine winning bid. Shill bidding and collusion detection is assumed to run as a pattern-matching layer over bid history, flagged for review rather than automatically blocking bids outright, since falsely blocking a genuine bidder is a worse outcome than a brief investigative delay.

blocks.text: A single popular item can realistically attract thousands of competing bidders across its entire listing window, with bidding activity concentrating heavily in the final minutes before the scheduled close, exactly the load pattern the anti-sniping mechanism exists to handle gracefully. Each individual proxy bid decision needs to complete in well under a second for the experience to feel genuinely live to bidders actively watching a closing auction.

The engine raises the current price only as much as needed to outbid the loser, and the close scheduler independently tracks whether this bid falls within the anti-sniping window, extending the closing time if so. Once the scheduler determines an auction has genuinely closed, the winning bid is handed to the payment service.

blocks.text: A bidder submits a single private maximum bid rather than manually re-bidding every time they are outbid. If this maximum does not exceed the current highest bidder's own private maximum, the current highest bidder stays winning and the price only rises enough to just outbid the new, losing bidder. If it does exceed the current highest bidder's maximum, the new bidder becomes the highest bidder, with the price rising only enough to just outbid the previous highest bidder's maximum, never jumping all the way to the new bidder's own true maximum.

blocks.text: Every bid is checked against the auction's current scheduled closing time. If it arrives within the anti-sniping window of that closing time, the closing time is pushed further out, giving other genuine bidders a real chance to respond. A bid arriving well before the window is left entirely unaffected.

class Auction:
    # An English auction: proxy bidding automatically raises the price only enough
    # to outbid the losing bidder's private maximum, and any bid arriving within
    # the anti-sniping window pushes the closing time further out.
    ANTI_SNIPE_WINDOW = 30
    EXTENSION_SECONDS = 60

    def __init__(self, starting_price, increment_amount, end_time):
        self.starting_price = starting_price
        self.increment_amount = increment_amount
        self.end_time = end_time
        self.current_price = starting_price
        self.current_winner = None
        self.current_winner_max_bid = 0

    def place_proxy_bid(self, bidder_id, max_bid, current_time):
        if current_time >= self.end_time:
            return f"{bidder_id}: AUCTION_CLOSED"

        if self.current_winner is None:
            self.current_winner = bidder_id
            self.current_winner_max_bid = max_bid
            self.current_price = self.starting_price
            result = f"{bidder_id}: WINNING at {self.current_price}"
        elif max_bid <= self.current_winner_max_bid:
            self.current_price = min(max_bid + self.increment_amount, self.current_winner_max_bid)
            result = f"{bidder_id}: OUTBID, current price now {self.current_price} held by {self.current_winner}"
        else:
            self.current_price = min(self.current_winner_max_bid + self.increment_amount, max_bid)
            self.current_winner = bidder_id
            self.current_winner_max_bid = max_bid
            result = f"{bidder_id}: WINNING at {self.current_price}"

        if self.end_time - current_time <= self.ANTI_SNIPE_WINDOW:
            self.end_time = current_time + self.EXTENSION_SECONDS  # anti-sniping: push the close further out
            result += f" (auction extended to {self.end_time})"
        return result

    def get_current_price(self):
        return self.current_price

    def get_current_winner(self):
        return self.current_winner

    def get_end_time(self):
        return self.end_time


def main():
    auction = Auction(100, 5, 1000)  # starting price 100, increment 5, closes at t=1000

    print(auction.place_proxy_bid("A", 150, 500))   # A: first bidder, winning at starting price
    print(auction.place_proxy_bid("B", 130, 600))   # B's max (130) <= A's max (150), A stays winning
    print(auction.place_proxy_bid("C", 200, 980))   # C's max (200) > A's max (150), C takes lead, extends close
    print(auction.place_proxy_bid("A", 250, 1030))  # A returns with a higher max, retakes lead, extends close again
    print(auction.place_proxy_bid("D", 300, 1100))  # arrives after the final extended close, correctly rejected

    print("Final price (should be 205):", auction.get_current_price())
    print("Final winner (should be A):", auction.get_current_winner())
    print("Final close time (should be 1090):", auction.get_end_time())

items: Architecture: proxy bidding that automatically raises the current price only enough to outbid a losing bidder's hidden maximum, paired with anti-sniping extension that pushes the closing time out for any bid arriving near it.
Capacity: a single popular item attracting thousands of competing bidders, with activity concentrating heavily in the final minutes before closing.
The core techniques: proxy bidding and anti-sniping extension, both worked through with a real, verified implementation in Java, Python, and C++.
Database: a single, unparallelized authoritative auction state per item made highly available through fast failover, alongside a durable, append-heavy bid history log.
End-to-end workflows: a normal proxy-bid flow and an anti-sniping extension flow, both traced as sequence diagrams.
Consistency: a strongly consistent, zero-tolerance-for-dual-winners auction state, paired with an eventually consistent watcher-facing display.
Trade-offs: proxy bidding with anti-sniping extension versus a fixed hard close versus manual-only bidding, compared directly on fairness against sniping and bidder experience.
